title: Quasi-finite = finite type + quasi-compact + finite fibres
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is
quasi-finite if and only if $f$ is
locally of finite type, of finite type, quasi-compact and has finite
fibres.
(*Stacks Project, Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 29.21.10, Tag
[02NH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02NH).*)

proof.text: For the forward implication, [pqf-def-quasifinite] says that $f$ is of finite type and every point of each fibre $X_s$ is isolated in $X_s$. By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], finite type implies that $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Fix $s\in S$. By [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] the base change $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is quasi-compact, so $X_s$, the preimage of the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, is quasi-compact. The singletons $\{\xi\}$, $\xi\in X_s$, are open and cover $X_s$, so a finite subcover exists and $X_s$ is a finite set. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the first projection maps $X_s$ bijectively (indeed homeomorphically) onto $f^{-1}(\{s\})$, so $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is finite.

proof.text: Conversely, assume $f$ is locally of finite type, quasi-compact, and has finite fibres; by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $f$ is of finite type. Let $x\in X$, $s=f(x)$, and choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni s$ of $S$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\ni x$ of $X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] the ring map $R\to A$ is of finite type, so $C=A\otimes_R\kappa(s)$ is a finitely generated $\kappa(s)$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with the opens $V\subseteq S$, $U\subseteq X$ and all of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$) the scheme $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is identified with the open subscheme $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$, where $p:X_s\to X$ is the first projection, and by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] $p$ is a homeomorphism onto $f^{-1}(\{s\})$, which is finite, so $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a finite space. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], applied to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $\kappa(s)$, the closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ lying in the closure $Z$ of any point $\eta$ are dense in $Z$; they form a finite, hence closed, set, so they exhaust $Z$ and $\eta$ is closed. Thus every point of the finite space $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is closed, every singleton is open, and the point $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=x$ is open in $p^{-1}(U)$, hence isolated in $X_s$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] gives that $R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of $x$, i.e. $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$ in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Thus $f$ is locally quasi-finite, and [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] gives that the locally quasi-finite quasi-compact morphism $f$ is quasi-finite.
